questions.question:
The general target of the monetary policy is to ensure ______.

A) price stability in the economy

B) greater tax collections for the government

C) employment generation in the rural areas
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Only A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monetary policy:-**

 
 
• It refers to the measures taken by the central bank of a country to regulate the supply of money and credit in the economy.
 
• The general target of the monetary policy is to ensure price stability in the economy.
 
• This means that the central bank aims to keep inflation low and stable, so that prices of goods and services do not fluctuate too much.
 
 
 
• **Inflation**:-
 
 
• It is a key concern for any economy, as it erodes the purchasing power of money and makes it difficult for people to plan their finances.
 
• The central bank uses various tools such as interest rates, reserve requirements, and open market operations to influence the supply of money and credit in the economy and keep inflation in check.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Price stability:
 
 
• Price stability means keeping inflation low and stable.

questions.question: Which of the following items is NOT a part of the non-plan revenue expenditure of the government budget?

options.text: Central assistance for states and union territories

• **Non-plan revenue expenditure:-**

 
 
• **It refers to the regular expenses incurred by the government in running its day-to-day operations and does not include any capital expenditures.**
 
• Salaries and pensions of government employees, subsidies to various sectors, and defense services are some of the major components of non-plan revenue expenditure. 
 
 
 
• **Central assistance:-**
 
 
• Central assistance for states and union territories, on the other hand, is a part of the plan expenditure, which refers to the government's spending on development and welfare schemes.
 
• Central assistance is provided to the states and union territories for specific purposes such as infrastructure development, poverty alleviation, and education.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Salaries and pensions: **

 
 
• This includes the salaries and pensions of government employees such as civil servants, police officers, and teachers.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies: **
 
 
• This refers to the financial assistance provided by the government to various sectors such as agriculture, industry, and exports, to promote their growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Defence services: **
 
 
• This includes the expenses incurred on the maintenance and modernization of the armed forces, as well as on border security and defense-related research and development.

questions.question: What did the term 'bhoga’ refer to during the medieval period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**revenue assignments.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhoga**:-

 
 
• It was a term used in medieval India to refer to the revenue assignments made by the state to its officials and other beneficiaries.
 
• These assignments were usually in the form of land or other resources, which could be used for agricultural or other purposes.
 
• The term bhoga was also used to refer to the income generated from such assignments, which could be in the form of taxes, rents, or other forms of payment.
 
 
 
• **Revenue assignments:-**
 
 
• These were a crucial part of the feudal system that existed in medieval India, where the state granted land and other resources to its officials and other beneficiaries in exchange for their loyalty and service.
 
• These assignments were often hereditary and could be passed down from generation to generation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Donations to temples:- **

 
 
• These were also common during the medieval period, but they were usually made by individuals or groups rather than the state. These donations could take the form of money, land, or other resources, and were often made as a way of earning religious merit or gaining social status.
 
 
 
• **Festival**:-
 
 
• Festivals and religious functions were important parts of medieval Indian society, but they were not directly related to the system of revenue assignments.
 
• It could also be referred to as bhoga in some contexts, but these were not the primary meanings of the term during the medieval period.

questions.question: The radius of curvature of a charged particle's passage in a homogeneous magnetic field is proportional to:

__
 
• **Radius of curvature of a charged particle's passage:-**

 
 
• The radius of curvature of a charged particle's passage in a homogeneous magnetic field is directly proportional to the momentum of the particle.
 
• This is because the magnetic force acting on the charged particle is perpendicular to both the direction of the magnetic field and the direction of the particle's velocity. This force causes the particle to move in a circular path with a radius proportional to its momentum.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The energy of the particle and the charge of the particle do not affect the radius of curvature in a homogeneous magnetic field.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field does affect the radius of curvature, but it is indirectly proportional rather than directly proportional. This means that as the magnetic field strength increases, the radius of curvature decreases.
 
• It is important to note that this relationship only holds true for a homogeneous magnetic field, where the field strength is constant throughout the region of interest.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary factor contributing to the dryness of old wells?

options.text: A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.
The ground surrounding the wells has been covered with a layer of vegetation,

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary factor contributing to dryness of old wells:**

 
 
• A lot of boring pumps have been set up in the adjacent areas, leading to depletion of groundwater resources and drying up of old wells.
 
• Groundwater depletion is a major issue in many parts of the world due to increasing population and demand for water.
 
• Wells being covered may contribute to their abandonment, but not necessarily to their dryness.
 
• People stopping to utilize wells may be a consequence of their dryness, not the cause.
 
• Vegetation around wells may actually help retain moisture and prevent evaporation, but it is not the primary factor contributing to their dryness. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Boring pumps extract groundwater from aquifers, which are underground layers of permeable rock or soil that hold water.
 
• Overuse of groundwater resources can lead to depletion and even collapse of aquifers, causing wells to dry up.
 
• Groundwater depletion can also have other negative impacts, such as land subsidence, saltwater intrusion, and reduced streamflow.
 
• In some cases, old wells can be rehabilitated by deepening or re-drilling them, or by implementing sustainable groundwater management practices.
